finalText:
All objectives complete. Final report:

**Goal: repair ticket flow — RunID fwrd94-n1**

1. **DONE** — Ticket titled "fwrd94-n1 RD Bench Ticket" created (customer Bench User), assigned reference **RD-1015** by the app. It appeared in the tickets list as a 14th ticket.

2. **DONE** — Part "fwrd94-n1 RD Part A" added with cost $100.00 and markup 25% (qty 1, supplier Bench Supply Co). The app computed a price of **$125.00** (100 + 25% markup).

3. **DONE** — Part "fwrd94-n1 RD Part B" added with cost $200.00 and markup 25% (qty 1, supplier Bench Supply Co). The app computed a price of **$250.00** (200 + 25% markup). Parts table total was $375.00.

4. **DONE** — Part A's cost edited from 100 to 150. The app recomputed its price to **$187.50** (150 + 25% markup); the row read: fwrd94-n1 RD Part A | $150.00 | 25% | 1 | Bench Supply Co | $187.50. Table total rose to $437.50.

5. **DONE** — Ticket RD-1015 is in status **Ready** (confirmed both on the detail page status chip and in the tickets list row "RD-1015 | ... | Ready | 2"). The precondition the app enforces: **at least one part must exist on the ticket** — verified by probing a separate zero-part Draft ticket (RD-1011), where "Mark Ready" was refused with the exact message "Ticket is not ready — A ticket needs at least one part before it can be marked Ready." Our ticket had two parts, so the precondition was already satisfied and no extra action was required to set Ready.

6. **DONE** — Both parts were deleted (each via a "Confirm" modal → "Delete part"), the parts table then showed "No parts on this ticket yet." The ticket was archived: the button changed to "Unarchive ticket", and in the list the active filter (search RD-1015) showed "No tickets match the current filters." while with "Show archived" checked the row appeared as "RD-1015 | fwrd94-n1 RD Bench Ticket Archived | Bench User | Ready | 0 | 2026-09-25". Nothing created by this run remains active.
